verdict.rationale: Solid's first-party README says global state management is built in through Context and Stores, so no third-party library is needed. It also documents reactive signals, derived state and automatic dependency tracking. A long-term user praises Solid's simple built-in state handling (no keys, deep state, no reducer) and its intuitive, immediate state changes on a large product. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the Store and Context APIs for global state (the evidence is limited to README-level claims).

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage global application state using built-in primitives without adding a third-party library

citations.quote: Performant state management is built-in with Context and Stores: you don't have to reach for a third party library to manage global state
Declare your state and use it throughout your app, and when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun.
Create a piece of reactive state, giving us an accessor, count(), and a setter, setCount()
